svg.aria-label: Belly band versus sleeve versus full printed box: three escalation levels of branding a plain box, band covering 20 to 30 percent, sleeve covering most, full print covering everything

g.text: Three escalation levels for branding a plain box
The economics follow the material — a strip, a panel, or a whole sheet wrapped on board
band — thin paper strip
BAND
covers about 20–30% of the face
one strip around the middle — least
material, message swappable per run
sleeve — thicker board panel
SLEEVE
wraps more of the box — often a full
perimeter or large slide-on panel,
on thicker board than a band
every surface printed
FULL PRINTED BOX
maximum brand surface, maximum print
cost — and the design is committed:
change the message, reprint the box
The ceiling test: past about a third of the face, a sleeve or a printed box is usually the better product.
The strategic use is versioning — one plain box stock, many bands: seasonal messages, limited runs, channel copy, base box unchanged.
Bands also do physical jobs: bundling multi-piece mailings into one neat bundle, and keeping packages from opening in transit or on display.
